title: Dynamics of the spontaneous emission factor in multiple quantum well nanowire lasers
authors: Parya Reyhanian, Christopher G Poulton, Arti Agrawal, Charlene J. Lobo
abstract: The spontaneous emission factor - often known as the \b{eta} factor - is an important quantity in the description of quantum well lasers, influencing both the threshold power as well as the general shape of the light in-light out (L-L) curve. Past work on modelling multiple quantum well (MQW) nanowire laser devices has typically assumed that the \b{eta} factor is a constant parameter that can either be estimated or fit in a post-hoc manner. However, the \b{eta} factor can be derived from the transitions between valence and conduction bands in semiconductor quantum wells, together with knowledge of the cavity modes. Here we investigate the dynamic nature of the \b{eta} factor for MQW nanowire lasers, and show how it can be computed. We also examine the dependence of the spontaneous emission rate and spontaneous emission factor \b{eta} on the charge carrier density, quantum well thickness, and composition, and discuss the impact on laser threshold and operation.
summary: This paper develops a theoretical framework to calculate the spontaneous emission factor ($ eta$) dynamically for MQW nanowire lasers, treating it as a variable rather than a constant. By coupling quantum electrodynamics with semiconductor physics, the authors show that $ eta$ strongly depends on carrier density, accurately predicting laser thresholds and spectral behavior near operation.
main_problem: The study investigates the dynamic nature of the spontaneous emission factor (the eta or beta factor) in multiple quantum well (MQW) nanowire lasers, moving beyond previous constant approximations.
main_result: The spontaneous emission factor is shown to be highly dependent on charge carrier density and device parameters, peaking near the lasing threshold before decreasing above it.
method: The authors derive general expressions for the beta factor and gain using quantum electrodynamics principles applied to semiconductor quantum wells, combining Finite Element Modeling (FEM) with rate equation analysis.
model_or_system: The system modeled is an MQW nanowire laser structure ($	ext{In}_{0.2}	ext{Ga}_{0.8}	ext{As}/	ext{GaAs}$), where the photonic density of states (PDOS) is calculated by combining free-space and discrete cavity Lorentzian modes.
key_observables: Spontaneous emission factor ($ eta$), laser gain, Lasing threshold power, and the spontaneous emission spectrum $	ext{r}_{	ext{spon}}(E)$.
important_parameters: Charge carrier density ($N_c$), quantum well thickness ($L_z$), Indium composition (In content), and cavity mode frequency.
main_assumptions: The model assumes that the cavity modes are sufficiently well-confined to be treated as discrete Lorentzian terms, and it utilizes Einstein coefficients for rate calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic structure of the laser, the total photonic density of states (PDOS), and crucially, plots showing $ eta$'s dependence on carrier density ($N_c$) relative to the lasing threshold.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical problem and deriving general theoretical expressions for $ eta$ using QED principles. It then applies this model to specific MQW nanowire structures, analyzing how varying carrier densities affects $ eta$, gain, and ultimately predicting the laser's operational characteristics like threshold power.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it models open quantum systems dynamics (spontaneous emission into a structured cavity) using rate equations derived from fundamental quantum electrodynamics principles, providing insights into light-matter interaction in nanoscale devices.
